title: The Sunday Read: ‘Has the Amazon Reached Its “Tipping Point”?’

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin, and I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 早在黑胶唱片时代我在夜店当DJ的时候，你每天晚上都要带300件你最珍爱的宝贝去工作，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你会把DJ台变成这样一个充满生活气息的快闪博物馆，里面摆满了精美的50岁老古董。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: The Amazon has been called the lungs of the earth.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊被誉为地球之肺。

sentences.en: It's the world's largest rainforest, where 400 billion trees constantly remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere as part of the process of photosynthesis.
sentences.zh: 它是世界上最大的热带雨林，有4000亿棵树木作为光合作用的一部分，不断从大气中吸收二氧化碳。

sentences.en: But there's this theory that's been around for the last few decades, that if enough of the Amazon is cut down,
sentences.zh: 但过去几十年里流传着这样一种理论：如果亚马逊被砍伐的面积足够大，

sentences.en: it could cross a tipping point and start to collapse into a degraded kind of savanna, a patchwork of grasslands, stunted little forests, and scrub.
sentences.zh: 它可能会越过一个引爆点，开始退化成某种稀树草原，由草地、矮小的森林和灌木丛交织而成。

sentences.en: It would be an ecosystem that does very little to compensate for the emissions created when we burn fossil fuels.
sentences.zh: 这将是一个几乎无法抵消我们燃烧化石燃料所产生排放的生态系统。

sentences.en: And in the last few years, scientists have observed strange transformations in the rainforeSt.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几年里，科学家们观察到雨林发生了奇怪的转变。

sentences.en: Signs that maybe this tipping point is now being reached.
sentences.zh: 种种迹象表明，这个引爆点可能正在到来。

sentences.en: My name's Alex Quadros.
sentences.zh: 我叫亚历克斯·夸德罗斯。

sentences.en: In this week's Sunday Read, you'll be hearing my story about the Amazon's tipping point that I wrote for the New York Times magazine.
sentences.zh: 在本周的“周日阅读”中，你将听到我为《纽约时报杂志》撰写的关于亚马逊引爆点的故事。

sentences.en: So, in 2022, I spent a couple of weeks following two scientists to see how the Amazon is changing.
sentences.zh: 因此，在2022年，我花了几周时间跟随两位科学家，看看亚马逊是如何变化的。

sentences.en: Luciana Gatchi is an atmospheric chemiSt.
sentences.zh: 露西亚娜·加奇是一位大气化学家。

sentences.en: She flies in bush plains over the forest to sample the air.
sentences.zh: 她乘坐丛林小飞机在森林上空飞行以采集空气样本。

sentences.en: And she has discovered that there's way, way too much carbon above the Amazon.
sentences.zh: 她发现亚马逊上空的碳实在是太多太多了。

sentences.en: That actually, parts of the rainforest are emitting more carbon than they're absorbing.
sentences.zh: 事实上，雨林的某些部分排放的碳比吸收的还要多。

sentences.en: Which may be the most disturbing sign that the ecosystem is malfunctioning.
sentences.zh: 这或许是生态系统发生故障最令人不安的迹象。

sentences.en: Olha como tá queimada essa árvore.
sentences.zh: 瞧瞧这棵树烧成什么样了。

sentences.en: Agora se imagina.
sentences.zh: 现在想象一下。

sentences.en: Together we met Erika Berenger, a biologist who's studying the effects of agriculture and wildfires on the rainforeSt.
sentences.zh: 我们一起见识了埃莉卡·贝伦格尔，一位研究农业和野火对雨林影响的生物学家。

sentences.en: But Erika also led us through what she called the David Attenborough Amazon.
sentences.zh: 但埃莉卡也带我们穿过了她所说的“大卫·爱登堡式的亚马逊”。

sentences.en: Those cliched, untouched, beautiful sections where centuries-old trees have trunks that can be wider than a person is tall.
sentences.zh: 那些陈旧、未受破坏、美丽绝伦的区域，那里的参天大树树干比一个人还要粗。

sentences.en: And it's funny because I realized that for all the time that I'd spent in the Amazon on previous reporting trips,
sentences.zh: 说来也巧，我意识到尽管我在以往的采访行程中在亚马逊度过了很长时间，

sentences.en: I'd never been to the areas that are barely touched by humans.
sentences.zh: 但我从未去过那些几乎未受人类触及的地区。

sentences.en: It showed me what the Amazon can be.
sentences.zh: 它向我展示了亚马逊本来的面貌。

sentences.en: And it was honestly moving.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这很感人。

sentences.en: In 2015, Erika watched as the embers from fires set to clear fields, something that farmers and ranchers do every year in the Amazon,
sentences.zh: 2015年，埃莉卡目睹了为清理土地而点燃的余烬——这是亚马逊的农民和牧场主每年都会做的事情——

sentences.en: started spreading into these miles-long arcs of fire that penetrated deep into the rainforeSt.
sentences.zh: 开始蔓延成数英里长的火弧，深入雨林腹地。

sentences.en: A lot of these massive old trees died, and vines and bamboo moved in, throwing the natural balance of species out of whack.
sentences.zh: 许多这些巨大的古树死了，藤蔓和竹子入侵，打破了物种的自然平衡。

sentences.en: The Amazon should be too wet for fires to spread on their own.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊本该足够湿润，不至于让火势自行蔓延。

sentences.en: But since the megafires in 2015, we've seen that's increasingly no longer the case.
sentences.zh: 但自从2015年的特大火灾以来，我们发现情况越来越不再如此。

sentences.en: And every time it burns, it's more prone to burning again, as dead trees and leaves dry out and fall to the ground.
sentences.zh: 而且每当它燃烧一次，就越容易再次燃烧，因为枯树和落叶变干并落到地面上。

sentences.en: Before reporting this story, I still had this image of scientists as coldly rational, people who don't get emotionally involved with their work.
sentences.zh: 在报道这个故事之前，我对科学家的印象仍然是冷酷理性的，是一群不会对自己的工作产生情感投入的人。

sentences.en: But actually, Erika told me that scientists have their own personal tipping points, when the situation feels so hopeless that they almost lose the will to continue working.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，埃莉卡告诉我，科学家们也有他们个人的引爆点，当情况变得如此绝望，以至于他们几乎失去了继续工作的意志。

sentences.en: When Luciana discovered that parts of the Amazon were emitting more carbon than they absorbed, she became depressed.
sentences.zh: 当露西亚娜发现亚马逊部分地区排放的碳多于吸收的碳时，她患上了抑郁症。

sentences.en: She thought about quitting and going to live in an eco-villa in the countryside with her German shepherd.
sentences.zh: 她考虑过辞职，带着她的德国牧羊犬去乡下的生态别墅生活。

sentences.en: At 62 years old, she could have actually retired two years ago.
sentences.zh: 62岁的她其实两年前就可以退休了。

sentences.en: But what's kept her going is knowing that her employer, a Brazilian government agency, has been so starved of resources that if she left, her lab could shut down,
sentences.zh: 但支撑她坚持下去的是，她知道她的雇主——一个巴西政府机构——资源匮乏，如果她离开，她的实验室可能会关门大吉，

sentences.en: leaving no one there to study the Amazon's mysterious carbon emissions.
sentences.zh: 从而没有人再去研究亚马逊神秘的碳排放。

sentences.en: So here's my article.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的文章。

sentences.en: Has the Amazon Reached Its Tipping Point?
sentences.zh: 亚马逊到达引爆点了吗？

sentences.en: One of the first times Luciana Vanigachi tried to collect Amazonian air, she got so woozy that she couldn't even operate the controls.
sentences.zh: 露西亚娜·瓦尼加奇第一次尝试收集亚马逊空气时，头晕得连控制杆都操作不了。

sentences.en: An atmospheric chemist, she wanted to measure the concentration of carbon high above the rainforeSt.
sentences.zh: 作为一名大气化学家，她想测量雨林高空的二氧化碳浓度。

sentences.en: To obtain her samples, she had to train bush pilots at obscure air taxi businesses.
sentences.zh: 为了获取样本，她不得不去偏僻的空中出租车公司培训丛林飞行员。

sentences.en: The discomfort began as she waited on the tarmac, holding one door open against the wind, to keep the tiny cockpit from turning into an oven in the equatorial sun.
sentences.zh: 这种不适从她在跑道上等待时就开始了，她用手顶着一扇门挡住强风，以免狭小的驾驶舱在赤道烈日下变成烤箱。

sentences.en: When at last they took off, they rose precipitously.
sentences.zh: 当他们终于起飞时，飞机急剧上升。

sentences.en: And every time they plunged into a cloud, the plane seemed to be, in Gachi's words,
sentences.zh: 每次他们冲入云层，飞机似乎都在用加奇的话说，

sentences.en: Sambamu, dancing the samba.
sentences.zh: Sambamu，跳着桑巴舞。

sentences.en: Then the air temperature dipped below freezing, and her sweat turned cold.
sentences.zh: 接着气温骤降至冰点以下，她的汗水变冷了。

sentences.en: Not that it was all bad.
sentences.zh: 倒也不是说全无美景。

sentences.en: As the frenetic port of Manaus receded, the canopy spread out below like a shaggy carpet,
sentences.zh: 随着狂热的马瑙斯港渐行渐远，树冠在下方展开，就像一张毛茸茸的地毯，

sentences.en: immaculate green except for the pink and yellow blooms of Ipe trees.
sentences.zh: 一尘不染的绿色中点缀着伊佩树粉色和黄色的花朵。

sentences.en: And it was one of those moments, increasingly rare in Gachi's experience,
sentences.zh: 这是那种在加奇的经历中越来越少见的时刻，

sentences.en: when you could pretend that nature had no final border, and the Amazon looked like what it somehow still was, the world's largest rainforeSt.
sentences.zh: 你可以假装自然没有最终的边界，亚马逊看起来依然像是它某种程度上仍然是的那个世界最大热带雨林。

sentences.en: The Amazon has been called the lungs of the Earth because of the amount of carbon dioxide it absorbs, according to most estimates, around half a billion tons per year.
sentences.zh: 根据大多数估计，由于亚马逊吸收的大约二氧化碳量（每年约有五亿吨），它被称为地球之肺。

sentences.en: The problem, scientifically speaking, is that these estimates have always depended on a series of extrapolations.
sentences.zh: 从科学上讲，问题在于这些估计一直依赖于一系列外推法。

sentences.en: Some researchers use satellites to detect changes that indicate the presence of greenhouse gases.
sentences.zh: 一些研究人员使用卫星来检测表明温室气体存在的变化。

sentences.en: But the method is indirect, and clouds can contaminate the results.
sentences.zh: 但这种方法是间接的，而且云层可能会污染结果。

sentences.en: Others start with individual tree measurements in plots scattered across the region, which allows them to calculate the so-called biomass in each trunk,
sentences.zh: 另一些人则从散布在该地区的样地中的单棵树木测量开始，这使他们能够计算出每根树干所谓的生物量，

sentences.en: which in turn allows them to work out how much carbon is being stored by the ecosystem as a whole.
sentences.zh: 进而算出整个生态系统储存了多少碳。

sentences.en: But it's hard to know how representative small study areas are because the Amazon is almost as large as the contiguous United States, with regional differences in rainfall,
sentences.zh: 但很难知道小型研究区域有多大代表性，因为亚马逊的面积几乎与美国本土一样大，在降雨量、

sentences.en: temperature, flora, and the extent of logging in agriculture.
sentences.zh: 温度、植物区系以及农业采伐程度方面都存在地区差异。

sentences.en: One study even warned of the risk of majestic forest selection bias.
sentences.zh: 一项研究甚至警告说存在雄伟森林选择偏差的风险。

sentences.en: Gachi's solution was to measure the carbon in the air directly, which led to the least pleasant part of the flight.
sentences.zh: 加奇的解决方案是直接测量空气中的碳，这也导致了飞行中最不愉快的一部分。

sentences.en: The pilot had removed the plane's back seats to make up for the weight of a special silver suitcase donated by the U.S.
sentences.zh: 飞行员拆掉了飞机的后排座位，以弥补美国国家海洋和大气管理局捐赠的一个特殊银色手提箱的重量。

sentences.en: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.
sentences.zh: 国家海洋和大气管理局。

sentences.en: Inside, a thick layer of foam cradled 17 glass flasks with valves that opened and closed at the flick of a switch.
sentences.zh: 里面有一层厚厚的海绵，保护着17个玻璃烧瓶，它们的阀门只需轻轻一拨就能打开和关闭。

sentences.en: Each one was supposed to capture a liter and a half of air from a different altitude, starting at 14,500 feet and going down to 1,000.
sentences.zh: 每个烧瓶都要从不同高度采集一升半的空气，从14500英尺开始一直降到1000英尺。

sentences.en: To ensure that collection always took place above the same point on the map, the pilot had to descend in tight spirals, banking so hard that the horizon went near vertical.
sentences.zh: 为了确保采集总是在地图上的同一点上方进行，飞行员不得不以紧密的螺旋形下降，倾斜度极大，以至于地平线几乎变成了垂直。

sentences.en: In a healthy rainforest, the concentration of carbon should decline as you approach the canopy from above because trees are drawing the element out of the atmosphere
sentences.zh: 在一个健康的雨林中，当你从上方接近树冠时，碳浓度应该会下降，因为树木正在从大气中吸取这种元素

sentences.en: and turning it into wood through photosynthesis.
sentences.zh: 并通过光合作用将其转化为木材。

sentences.en: In 2010, when Gachi started running two flights a month at each of four different spots in the Brazilian Amazon, she expected to confirm this.
sentences.zh: 2010年，当加奇开始在巴西亚马逊的四个不同地点的每一个地方每月进行两次飞行时，她本以为会证实这一点。

sentences.en: But her samples showed the opposite.
sentences.zh: 但她的样本显示的情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: At lower altitudes, the ratio of carbon increased.
sentences.zh: 在较低海拔地区，碳的比例有所增加。

sentences.en: This suggested that emissions from the slashing and burning of trees, the preferred method for clearing fields in the Amazon, were actually exceeding the forest's capacity
sentences.zh: 这表明，砍伐和焚烧树木（亚马逊清理土地的首选方法）产生的排放实际上已经超出了森林

sentences.en: to absorb carbon.
sentences.zh: 吸收碳的能力。

sentences.en: At first,
sentences.zh: 起初，

sentences.en: Gachi was sure it was an anomaly caused by a passing drought.
sentences.zh: 加奇确信这是由过往干旱引起的异常现象。

sentences.en: But the trend not only persisted into wetter years, it intensified.
sentences.zh: 但这种趋势不仅在较湿润的年份持续存在，而且愈演愈烈。

sentences.en: For a while,
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，

sentences.en: Gachi simply refused to believe her own data.
sentences.zh: 加奇简直拒绝相信自己的数据。

sentences.en: She even became depressed.
sentences.zh: 她甚至陷入了抑郁。

sentences.en: She had always felt a deep connection to nature.
sentences.zh: 她一直对大自然怀有深厚的感情。

sentences.en: As a kid in a distant town called Cafelangia, she would climb a tree in front of her house, spending hours in a formation of branches that seemed custom-made to cradle her arms,
sentences.zh: 小时候在一个叫卡费兰迪亚的偏远小镇，她会爬上房前的一棵树，在树枝间度过几个小时，那些树枝的形状似乎是专门为了托住她的手臂、

sentences.en: legs, and head.
sentences.zh: 双腿和头部而生。

sentences.en: In later years, no matter how many times she flew over the Amazon, she never got used to the sight of freshly paved highways, new dirt roads always branching off them,
sentences.zh: 在后来的岁月里，无论她飞越亚马逊多少次，她都习惯不了那些新铺设的高速公路、从它们分叉出的源源不断的新泥路，

sentences.en: forming a fishbone pattern.
sentences.zh: 形成鱼骨状的图案。

sentences.en: Sometimes she soared past columns of beige smoke that rose all the way to the stratosphere.
sentences.zh: 有时她从直冲平流层的米色烟柱旁飞过。

sentences.en: Back at her laboratory, which is now housed at Brazil's
sentences.zh: 回到她的实验室，该实验室现在设在巴西

sentences.en: National Institute for Space Research,
sentences.zh: 国家空间研究所，

sentences.en: IMPI,
sentences.zh: INPE，

sentences.en: Gachi ultimately spent two years refining her methodology.
sentences.zh: 加奇最终花了两年时间完善她的方法论。

sentences.en: She wanted to know just how much carbon the rainforest was losing, and even more important, how representative these results were.
sentences.zh: 她想知道雨林到底损失了多少碳，更重要的是，这些结果具有多大的代表性。

sentences.en: The whole point of her project was that by capturing air from such high altitudes, it could provide an empirical and comprehensive picture of the Amazon's so-called carbon budget.
sentences.zh: 她这个项目的全部意义在于，通过从如此高的高度捕获空气，它可以提供亚马逊所谓碳预算的实证和全面图景。

sentences.en: So she worked up seven different ways to calculate the effect of wind flows and the composition of air from over the Atlantic Ocean, gradually perfecting her method for subtracting
sentences.zh: 因此，她研究出了七种不同的方法来计算风流的影响以及来自大西洋上空的空气成分，逐渐完善了她减去

sentences.en: the background noise.
sentences.zh: 背景噪声的方法。

sentences.en: Finally, she felt confident that her regions of influence captured what was happening across 80% of the Amazon.
sentences.zh: 最后，她确信她的影响区域捕捉到了亚马逊80%地区正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: The net emissions averaged nearly
sentences.zh: 净排放量平均每年近

sentences.en: 300 million tons of carbon per year, roughly the emissions of the entire nation of France.
sentences.zh: 3亿吨碳，大约相当于整个法国的排放量。

sentences.en: When Gachi published her findings in Nature in 2021, it sparked panicked headlines across the world.
sentences.zh: 当加奇于2021年在《自然》杂志上发表她的发现时，它在全世界引发了惊恐的头条新闻。

sentences.en: The lungs of the Earth are exhaling greenhouse gases.
sentences.zh: 地球之肺正在呼出温室气体。

sentences.en: But her discovery was actually much more alarming than that.
sentences.zh: 但她的发现实际上比这更加令人担忧。

sentences.en: Because burning trees release a high proportion of carbon monoxide, she could separate these emissions from the total.
sentences.zh: 因为燃烧的树木会释放出高比例的一氧化碳，她可以将这些排放物与总量分开。

sentences.en: And in the southeastern Amazon, air samples still showed net emissions, suggesting that the ecosystem itself could be releasing more carbon than it absorbed, or in Gachi's words,
sentences.zh: 在亚马逊东南部，空气样本仍然显示净排放量，这表明生态系统本身释放的碳可能多于吸收的碳，用加奇的话说，

sentences.en: effectively dying more than growing.
sentences.zh: 实际上是死去的比生长的多。

sentences.en: The first time I spoke to Gachi, she repurposed a lyric by the
sentences.zh: 我第一次和加奇交谈时，她引用了巴西歌手

sentences.en: Brazilian crooner
sentences.zh: 乔治·本-若尔

sentences.en: Giorgi Ben-Jor.
sentences.zh: 的一句歌词。

sentences.zh: 最终，我们离开公路，驶入了一条以一堵植被墙结束的未标明土路。

sentences.zh: 贝伦格尔手持大砍刀，带领我们走上一条狭窄的小路。

sentences.en: Just a few days earlier, she and her assistant spent hours clearing the way for us, but new vines were already reclaiming the space.
sentences.zh: 就在几天前，她和她的助手还花了好几个小时为我们清理道路，但新的藤蔓已经重新占领了这片空间。

sentences.en: You can see it's a mess,
sentences.zh: 你可以看到这是一团糟，

sentences.en: Berenguer said.
sentences.zh: 贝伦格尔说。

sentences.zh: 一片密不透风的芦苇状竹丛从两边包围着我们。

sentences.en: The canopy was low above our heads.
sentences.zh: 树冠在我们头顶很低。

sentences.en: To me, it looked normal enough, as far as jungle goes.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，就丛林而言，它看起来很正常。

sentences.en: In reality, though, a healthy rainforest should be easy to walk through, because the largest trees consume so much light and water that the understory lacks the resources
sentences.zh: 但实际上，健康的雨林应该很容易穿行，因为最大的树木消耗了那么多的光照和水分，以至于林下层缺乏资源

sentences.en: to grow very dense.
sentences.zh: 长得非常茂密。

sentences.en: We walked over fallen trunks.
sentences.zh: 我们从倒下的树干上走过。

sentences.en: Unlike in the southeastern
sentences.zh: 与东南部的

sentences.zh: 亚马孙不同，贝伦格尔仍然没有看到类似稀树草原的植被入侵的迹象。

sentences.en: But the balance of native species was now out of whack.
sentences.zh: 但本地物种的平衡现在已经失衡了。

sentences.en: As opportunistic pioneers occupied the spaces left by dead giants.
sentences.zh: 当机会主义的先锋物种占据了死去的参天大树留下的空间时。

sentences.en: In some areas, fast-growing imbauba trees stood so uniformly that they resembled the stems of a wood pulp plantation.
sentences.zh: 在某些地区，生长迅速的伞树排列得如此均匀，以至于它们类似于木浆种植园的茎。

sentences.en: In others, hundreds of newborn lianas formed a kind of snake neSt.
sentences.zh: 在另一些地方，数百株新生的藤本植物形成了一种蛇窝。

sentences.en: Berenguer's team had to measure each one individually, a hellish task.
sentences.zh: 贝伦格尔的团队必须单独测量每一个，这是一项地狱般的工作。

sentences.en: She pointed to a tall, proud tree that had somehow survived the blaze.
sentences.zh: 她指着一棵高大、骄傲的树，它不知怎么在烈火中幸存了下来。

sentences.en: Because all of the other nearby individuals of its species had been killed, it was unlikely to reproduce.
sentences.zh: 因为附近该物种的所有其他个体都已被杀死，它不太可能繁殖。

sentences.en: Berenguer called it a zombie.
sentences.zh: 贝伦格尔称之为僵尸。

sentences.en: Even in the absence of actual savannization, trees that can withstand drier conditions are proliferating, while those that need more water are dying in greater numbers.
sentences.zh: 即使没有真正的稀树草原化，能够耐受更干燥条件的树木也在激增，而那些需要更多水分的树木则在大量死亡。

sentences.en: The dominance of imbauba is particularly worrisome because the trees are hollow, storing far less carbon than a slower-growing species like mahogany.
sentences.zh: 伞树的统治地位尤其令人担忧，因为这些树是中空的，储存的碳远少于像红木这样生长较慢的物种。

sentences.en: Their life cycle is also relatively short, leaving more frequent gaps in the canopy.
sentences.zh: 它们的生命周期也相对较短，在树冠中留下了更频繁的空隙。

sentences.en: The end result of this transformation is unclear.
sentences.zh: 这一转变的最终结果目前尚不明确。

sentences.en: But Gachi's numbers have only continued to get worse.
sentences.zh: 但加奇的数据却一直在恶化。

sentences.en: According to her latest five-year averages, the Brazilian Amazon is already giving off 50% more carbon than it was in the first five years of her project.
sentences.zh: 根据她最新的五年平均数据，巴西亚马逊地区的碳排放量已经比她项目开展的前五年高出了50%。

sentences.en: And even the historically healthier western forests are sometimes emitting more than they absorb.
sentences.zh: 甚至连历史上生态更健康的西部森林，有时排放的碳也超过了它们吸收的碳。

sentences.en: Eventually, we came into a clearing.
sentences.zh: 最终，我们来到了一片林间空地。

sentences.en: I began to sweat.
sentences.zh: 我开始出汗。

sentences.en: The sun was searing hot.
sentences.zh: 太阳炙烤得厉害。

sentences.en: Berenguer said that unshaded ground can reach 176 degrees Fahrenheit here.
sentences.zh: 贝伦格尔说，这里的无荫地面温度可达176华氏度。

sentences.en: Clearings are a natural part of the
sentences.zh: 林间空地是亚马逊自然循环的

sentences.en: Amazonian cycle, as large trees inevitably die and other species gradually take their place.
sentences.zh: 一部分，因为大树难免会枯死，其他物种则会逐渐取而代之。

sentences.en: But even logging could not match the power of fire to turn the forest into Swiss cheese.
sentences.zh: 但即便是伐木，其将森林变成瑞士奶酪般满目疮痍的力量也无法与火灾相提并论。

sentences.en: Berenguer never used to need sunscreen because the canopy was so thick.
sentences.zh: 贝伦格尔以前从不需要防晒霜，因为树冠实在是太浓密了。

sentences.en: Now she gets sunburned here.
sentences.zh: 现在她在这里都会被晒伤。

sentences.en: And the profusion of holes sets off a vicious cycle.
sentences.zh: 而密集的空洞则引发了恶性循环。

sentences.en: The sun dries out the vegetation.
sentences.zh: 阳光烤干了植被。

sentences.en: Trees shed leaves to preserve water.
sentences.zh: 树木为了保存水分而落叶。

sentences.en: The litter becomes fuel for the next fire.
sentences.zh: 这些落叶成了下一场大火的燃料。

sentences.en: The gaps also create a wind corridor, allowing strong drafts to penetrate deep into the forest during storMs.
sentences.zh: 林间空隙还形成了一条风廊，使强风能够在暴风雨期间深入森林内部。

sentences.en: Perversely, with their heavy trunks, the largest, oldest trees are especially vulnerable to being knocked over.
sentences.zh: 令人反常的是，由于树干沉重，那些最大、最古老的树木特别容易被刮倒。

sentences.en: This used to be a beautiful forest,
sentences.zh: 这里曾经是一片美丽的森林，

sentences.en: Sharofi said.
sentences.zh: 沙罗菲说。

sentences.en: Some days it makes me sad,
sentences.zh: 有时候这让我很难过，

sentences.en: Berenguer said.
sentences.zh: 贝伦格尔说。

sentences.en: Other days it pisses me off.
sentences.zh: 有时候这让我火冒三丈。

sentences.en: This is one of those days.
sentences.zh: 今天就是其中之一。

sentences.en: Berenguer had hoped that the misfortune of the megafire would at least provide an opportunity to study how a rainforest recovers from such disgrace.
sentences.zh: 贝伦格尔原本希望，特大火灾的不幸至少能提供一个契机，去研究热带雨林如何从这般浩劫中恢复过来。

sentences.en: But she worried that she would never find out, because it would never get the chance.
sentences.zh: 但她担心自己永远也找不到答案，因为森林根本不会得到这样的机会。

sentences.en: Among scientists who study the Amazon, the notion of multiple tipping points specific to each region's ecology has increasingly taken hold.
sentences.zh: 在研究亚马逊的科学家中，针对每个地区生态特异性的多个临界点的概念已经越来越深入人心。

sentences.en: And some now speak of an even more urgent flammability tipping point, past which an ecosystem that never evolved to burn starts burning regularly.
sentences.zh: 有些人现在甚至谈到了一个更加紧迫的可燃性临界点，一旦跨越这个点，一个从未进化出适应火灾机制的生态系统就会开始频繁起火。

sentences.en: During the drought of 2015, wildfires also ravaged another nearby conservation area, the Reserva Extrachivista Tapajos
sentences.zh: 在2015年的旱灾期间，野火还肆虐了另一个附近的自然保护区——塔帕若斯

sentences.en: Arapiuns.

sentences.en: Because it was left so degraded, with so much dried-out fuel on the floor, there was a much more intense conflagration in 2017, even though that was a wet year.
sentences.zh: 由于该地区受损严重，地面堆积了大量干燥的燃料，因而在2017年引发了一场更为猛烈的大火，尽管那是一个多雨的年份。

sentences.en: This time the flames were not the foot-tall ones that are usually seen in the Amazon, but reached all the way to the canopy.
sentences.zh: 这一次的火焰不再是亚马逊常见的盈尺之火，而是直冲树冠。

sentences.en: Though her mainstay was ecological calamity, Berenguer also wanted us to see what well-preserved old-growth forest looks like.
sentences.zh: 尽管她的主要研究对象是生态灾难，但贝伦格尔也希望让我们看看保存完好的原始森林是什么样子的。

sentences.en: In strictly scientific terms, it was a control, a necessary point of comparison with the messed-up forests, as she called them, though she used a more colorful word that cannot be
sentences.zh: 用严格的科学术语来说，这是一个对照组，是与她口中那些“搞砸了的森林”进行对比的必要参照，尽管她用了一个更加生动、无法在此

sentences.en: printed here.
sentences.zh: 刊登的词汇。

sentences.en: She also let on that she welcomed the rare excuse to traipse around a more

sentences.en: David Attenborough setting.
sentences.zh: 大卫·爱登堡纪录片布景的地方闲逛。

sentences.en: So we drove south on the BR-163 until we hit the 117th-kilometer marker, where we re-entered the Tapajos.
sentences.zh: 于是我们沿着BR-163公路向南行驶，直到到达117公里处路标，在那里我们重新进入了塔帕若斯森林。

sentences.en: We were walking for only a few minutes before the difference became obvious.
sentences.zh: 我们只走了几分钟，差异就变得显而易见。

sentences.en: It was cooler and darker.
sentences.zh: 这里更凉爽，也更阴暗。

sentences.en: The flora was far more varied, forming distinct layers as you lifted your eyes to the sky.
sentences.zh: 植物种类要丰富得多，当你把视线投向天空时，会发现它们形成了清晰的层次。

sentences.en: The canopy was far more closed, the understory far more open.
sentences.zh: 树冠要闭合得多，而下层植被则开阔得多。

sentences.en: Berenguer and Sharope didn't even need to prune the trail for our visit.
sentences.zh: 贝伦格尔和沙罗佩甚至不需要为我们的参观修剪小径。

sentences.en: There were lianas here, too, but they were few and large.
sentences.zh: 这里也有藤本植物，但数量少而粗大。

sentences.en: One was as thick as a tree.
sentences.zh: 其中有一根像树干一样粗。

sentences.en: Berenguer said it was probably centuries old.
sentences.zh: 贝伦格尔说它可能已经有几个世纪的历史了。

sentences.en: It's hard to shake a popular image of scientists as rigorously rational, unemotional about their work.
sentences.zh: 人们很难摆脱这样一种刻板印象，即科学家总是严谨理性，对自己的工作毫无情感波动。

sentences.en: But Berenguer was not embarrassed to admit that, as she put it, she and her colleagues have their own personal tipping points, too.
sentences.zh: 但贝伦格尔并不不好意思承认，正如她所说，她和同事们也有他们自己的个人情绪临界点。

sentences.en: For a while after the 2015 fires, she lost her sense of purpose, the hope that her work could make a difference.
sentences.zh: 在2015年大火之后的很长一段时间里，她失去了目标感，失去了对自己的工作能够带来改变的希望。

sentences.en: The flames had even ravaged the plot where she used to swing on that perfect loop of liana.
sentences.zh: 大火甚至摧毁了她曾经在那根完美的藤蔓上荡秋千的那片林地。

sentences.en: Your whole reference system is being destroyed, and you're powerless, she said.
sentences.zh: 你整个的参考体系正在被摧毁，而你却无能为力，她说。

sentences.en: It's hard to explain without sounding like a tree hugger.
sentences.zh: 这很难解释，除非听起来像个环保主义者。

sentences.en: Not to say I don't hug trees, because I do.
sentences.zh: 并不是说我不抱抱树，因为我确实会这样做。

sentences.en: Some trees were too big for that, though.
sentences.zh: 不过有些树太大了，抱不过来。

sentences.en: Here was an urukurana, with its wing-like buttress roots taller than my whole body.
sentences.zh: 这里有一棵乌鲁库拉纳树，它那翼状的板根比我的整个人还要高。

sentences.en: Here was a soaring strangler fig, which surrounds another tree's trunk as it grows, eventually killing its hoSt.
sentences.zh: 这里有一株高耸的绞杀榕，它在生长过程中缠绕着另一棵树的树干，最终会杀死它的寄主。

sentences.en: What a dirty trick, Gachi exclaimed.
sentences.zh: 真是个卑鄙的把戏，加奇惊叹道。

sentences.zh: 这有毒吗？

sentences.zh: 我不知道，沙罗佩说。

sentences.zh: 接着他从树枝上摘下一个，咬了一口。

sentences.en: We did the same.

sentences.zh: 果核周围并没有多少果肉，但味道辛辣而浓郁。

sentences.en: Berenguer remembered a past research trip to track frugivores, fruit-eating creatures.
sentences.zh: 贝伦格尔想起过去的一次研究之旅，当时是为了追踪食果动物。

sentences.en: She and her colleagues had to remain absolutely still and silent for hours to avoid spooking them.
sentences.zh: 她和同事们必须一动不动、安安静静地呆上几个小时，以免惊吓到它们。

sentences.en: I suggest that we try it out for a minute, just to hear what an old-growth forest sounds like without humans tramping around.
sentences.zh: 我建议我们试着体验一分钟，只是为了听听没有人类践踏的原始森林是什么声音。

sentences.en: We stopped walking.
sentences.zh: 我们停下脚步。

sentences.en: Berenguer sat on a log.
sentences.zh: 贝伦格尔坐在一根木头上。

sentences.en: As our chitchat faded, the racket of birds swelled as if someone had suddenly turned the volume dial on a stereo.
sentences.zh: 随着我们的闲聊声渐渐消退，鸟儿的鸣叫声骤然高涨，就像有人突然调大了立体声音响的音量。

sentences.en: I closed my eyes for a moment.
sentences.zh: 我闭上眼睛一会儿。

sentences.en: When I looked again, Berenguer's eyes had narrowed to slits.
sentences.zh: 当我再次睁开眼时，贝伦格尔的眼睛已经眯成了一条缝。

sentences.en: Her lips curled into a faint smile.
sentences.zh: 她的嘴角泛起一丝淡淡的微笑。

sentences.en: Earlier, describing what she felt in this place, Berenguer used the word grandiza, which literally means greatness, but also bigness.
sentences.zh: 此前，在描述她在这个地方的感受时，贝伦格尔用了“grandiza”这个词，字面意思是伟大，但也有巨大之意。

sentences.en: The rain forest made her feel small, and she liked this.
sentences.zh: 这片热带雨林让她觉得自己很渺小，而她很喜欢这种感觉。

sentences.en: God, she had spoken about feeling, at least temporarily, not so separate from the natural world, almost as if she were a kid again, ensconced in that tree in front of her house.
sentences.zh: 天哪，她谈到了一种感觉，至少在暂时觉得她与自然界并不是那么隔绝，几乎就像她又回到了小时候，坐在自己房子前面的那棵树里。

sentences.en: Now she stood with her eyes shut, palms open at her sides, as if she were at a religious revival, as if she were receiving something.
sentences.zh: 现在她闭着双眼站在那里，双臂垂在身侧、手掌朝外，就像身处一场宗教复兴集会，仿佛正在接受某种洗礼。
